slides.0.subtitle: Level 1 · Module 1 · Lesson 1
slides.1.title: Australia's Six Wine-Producing States
slides.1.subtitle: SA · VIC · NSW · WA · TAS · QLD — a wine continent spanning 100+ GIs
slides.2.title: Australia's Place in the Global Wine Market
slides.2.points.0: 5th largest wine exporter globally (2023 export value: A$1.8 billion)
slides.2.points.1: Approximately 145,000 hectares under vine across 6 states + territories
slides.2.points.3: Annual production: ~1.3 billion bottles, with 70% exported
slides.2.points.4: Top export markets: UK, USA, China, Canada
slides.2.note: Although Australia is a New World wine country, its winemaking history dates back to 1788 with British colonisation
slides.3.title: Six Defining Characteristics of Australian Wine
slides.3.points.0: 🌡️ Diverse climates: from cool maritime Tasmania to hot continental Barossa — an enormous spectrum
slides.3.points.1: 🍇 Variety of grapes: from Shiraz, Cabernet and Chardonnay to Italian and Portuguese varieties
slides.3.points.2: 🔩 Technical innovation: pioneer of the Stelvin screwcap closure, world leader in winemaking technology
slides.3.points.3: 🌱 Sustainable viticulture: organic and biodynamic farming growing fast; Bush vine old-vine preservation
slides.3.points.4: 🏆 Outstanding value: from everyday supermarket wines to world-class collectibles — wide price range
slides.3.points.5: 🌏 Cultural fusion: diverse European immigrant traditions — Italian, German and French influences coexist
slides.4.title: Industry Structure and Trade
slides.4.points.0: Small producers dominate: ~2,600 producers nationwide, but only 16 crush over 10,000 tonnes a year
slides.4.points.1: Wine Australia: the statutory industry body, funded by a grower/producer levy — runs R&D, export control, marketing and education
slides.4.points.2: Top 5 companies: Casella Family Brands (Yellow Tail), Treasury Wine Estates (Penfolds), Accolade Wines, Australian Vintage, Pernod Ricard
slides.4.points.3: China dispute: China accounted for 42% of Australian wine export value in 2019; in 2020 China imposed steep anti-dumping tariffs, upending the export market overnight
slides.4.points.4: Direct-to-consumer (D2C): cellar door sales can reach 70% of revenue for small wineries vs. only ~4% for large companies; the rest flows through websites and wine clubs
slides.4.note: The industry relies heavily on exports and is dominated by a handful of large groups, yet its base remains thousands of small family wineries
slides.5.question: What is Australia's rank among global wine exporters?
slides.5.explanation: Australia is the world's 5th largest wine exporter. Its primary markets are the UK, USA and China.
slides.6.title: Lesson Summary
slides.6.points.0: Australia is a major wine exporting nation — annual exports worth A$1.8 billion
slides.6.points.1: Spans multiple climate zones; remarkable diversity of varieties and styles
slides.6.points.2: Renowned for technological innovation (screwcap) and outstanding value for money
slides.6.points.3: Dominated by small wineries, yet exports are concentrated in a few markets like China — a real trade-policy vulnerability
